source_records.title: Direction-Aware Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks with Dual-Conditioned Normalizing Flows for Spatio-Temporal Anomaly Detection
source_records.abstract: Spatio-temporal graph neural networks on directed heterogeneous graphs face two structural challenges: symmetric graph aggregations cannot distinguish directional propagation mechanisms, and pure likelihood-based density scoring can underweight sparse localized perturbations. We address both within DA-GTNF, a unified framework for freeway anomaly detection. First, a direction-aware heterogeneous graph explicitly encodes four asymmetric relation types (downstream propagation, upstream shockwave, lateral lane interaction, and diagonal lane change), enabling a Relational GCN to learn independent aggregation kernels per relation. Second, a DualBranchGating mechanism fuses spatial graph embeddings and temporal Transformer embeddings through adaptive, feature-wise gates derived from unfused outputs. Third, a Dual-Conditioned Normalizing Flow estimates exact token-wise conditional log-likelihoods of the gated embeddings, while an auxiliary reconstruction head improves sensitivity to micro-level deviations that may be weakly reflected by NLL alone. On FT-AED, DA-GTNF achieves an AUC of 0.7218, a Reporting Delay of −11.80 min, a Mean Localization Error of 2.23 miles, and 100% incident coverage. On PeMS with incomplete ground truth, the segment-level DA-GTNF variant also consistently improves Recall@K% over all compared baselines.

source_records.title: Epidemiology-Informed Graph Neural Network for Heterogeneity-Aware Epidemic Forecasting
source_records.abstract: Among various spatio-temporal prediction tasks, epidemic forecasting plays a critical role in public health management. Recent studies have demonstrated the strong potential of spatio-temporal graph neural networks in extracting heterogeneous spatio-temporal patterns for epidemic forecasting. However, most of these methods bear an oversimplified assumption that two locations (e.g., cities) with similar observed features in previous time steps will develop similar infection numbers in the future. In fact, for any epidemic disease, there exists strong heterogeneity of its latent transmission dynamics across both geolocation and time, which can eventually lead to diverged infection numbers in two “similar” locations. However, capturing such latent transmission heterogeneity is non-trivial due to the existence of numerous influencing factors like medical resource accessibility, virus mutations, mobility patterns, etc., most of which are spatio-temporal yet unreachable or even unobservable. To address this challenge, we propose a Heterogeneous Epidemic-Aware Transmission Graph Neural Network (HeatGNN), a novel epidemic forecasting framework. By integrating epidemiological modeling into a Graph Neural Network, HeatGNN learns epidemiology-informed location embeddings of different locations that reflect their own transmission dynamics over time. On top of the conventional spatio-temporal module, a heterogeneous transmission graph network is designed to uncover the latent transmission heterogeneity among locations, where the time-varying latent transmission affinity graphs are computed on-the-fly and provide additional predictive signals. Experiments (Code is available at https://github.com/YufanZheng/HeatGNN_ECML-PKDD .) on four benchmark datasets have revealed that HeatGNN outperforms various strong baselines.

source_records.title: Utility-Aware Runtime Assessment of Sensor Selection Based on Spatio-Temporal Dynamic Graph Learning
source_records.abstract: With the rapid development of IoT technologies and widespread deployment of intelligent sensing devices, dynamic sensor selection has become crucial for balancing recognition accuracy and energy efficiency in applications like health monitoring. Existing runtime assessment methods suffer from limited predictive utility for future sensor quality and fail to capture dynamic spatio-temporal dependencies among interconnected devices. To this end, we propose a utility-aware sensor selection framework that integrates adaptive spatio-temporal forecasting with attention-based quality assessment. Our approach employs a Dynamic Graph Learning-based Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (DGL-STGCN) to model evolving device correlations and predict sensor states, while an attention mechanism assesses future sensor utility through learned importance scores. This enables proactive sensor selection optimized for both recognition accuracy and energy consumption, explicitly accounting for switching overheads. We develop and evaluate a prototype system designed for wearable devices to monitor locomotion activities. Results show that our system achieves a 14% accuracy improvement over single-sensor baselines, a 25% reduction in energy consumption compared to full-sensor deployment, and a 2% higher accuracy than state-of-the-art methods at equivalent energy levels.

source_records.title: HBPC-GWN: Hierarchical Bayesian Calibration for Graph-Based Traffic Forecasting
source_records.abstract: Accurate traffic forecasting requires effective modeling of complex spatio-temporal dependencies and reliable uncertainty estimation. Although existing graph-based methods have achieved strong performance, most focus on deterministic prediction and do not explicitly incorporate structural information into probabilistic modeling. In this paper, we propose HBPC-GWN, a hierarchical Bayesian calibration framework for graph-based traffic forecasting. Rather than imposing structural constraints during training, the proposed method performs posterior-level calibration by integrating a Laplacian-based prior into the predictive distribution. This enables a principled combination of data-driven predictions and graph-structured regularization, improving the consistency between spatial structure and uncertainty estimation. We instantiate the framework on Graph WaveNet and evaluate it on multiple real-world traffic datasets. Experimental results show that HBPC-GWN achieves competitive and more stable performance across forecasting horizons. In particular, it provides consistent improvements in medium- and long-term forecasting and improves probabilistic calibration, as reflected by better negative log-likelihood and prediction interval coverage. These results demonstrate that incorporating structural priors at the posterior level is an effective and flexible strategy for enhancing both predictive accuracy and uncertainty estimation in traffic forecasting.

source_records.title: A Physics-Informed Spatio-temporal Graph Learning Framework for EV Charging Demand Forecasting
source_records.abstract: Accurate forecasting of electric vehicle (EV) charging demand is essential for maintaining power-grid stability and supporting the efficient operation of urban charging infrastructure. However, EV charging demand exhibits strong spatio-temporal heterogeneity, multi-scale fluctuations, and complex dependencies, making accurate forecasting challenging. To address these issues, this paper proposes a physics-informed spatio-temporal graph learning framework for EV charging demand forecasting. Specifically, PSO-optimized MVMD is used to reconstruct multi-regional occupancy sequences, while a 2D-CNN is employed to capture temporal interaction patterns between occupancy and electricity price. A GAT-GFC-BiGRU-TPA architecture is then developed to model spatial dependencies and key temporal dynamics across charging regions. In addition, a physics-informed meta-learning strategy with a price-sensitivity regularization term is introduced to better capture the demand-response relationship between charging demand and electricity price while improving cross-region adaptability and training stability. Experiments on a real-world EV charging dataset show that the proposed framework consistently outperforms competitive baselines across multiple forecasting horizons. Ablation studies further verify the effectiveness of the major components. Overall, the proposed framework effectively captures complex spatio-temporal dynamics and improves short- and medium-term EV charging demand forecasting.

source_records.title: Dynamic Spatiotemporal Graph Learning of EEG for Multi-type Epileptiform Event Detection
source_records.abstract: Multi-type epileptiform events, including spike and ripple activities in electroencephalogram (EEG), are important biomarkers for seizure detection; however, their accurate detection is challenging due to complex spatio-temporal dynamics and multi-scale oscillatory patterns. To address these challenges, we propose a unified framework that integrates clinically motivated multi-band decomposition with dynamic spatio-temporal representation learning for accurate classification of EEG signals. Specifically, EEG signals are first decomposed into multiple frequency branches, followed by a branch-aware wavelet enhancement module to emphasize transient oscillatory patterns. A multi-scale temporal convolution module is then employed to capture diverse temporal dynamics across different time scales. Finally, a dynamic spatio-temporal graph reasoning module constructs sample-adaptive spatial and temporal graphs and performs joint propagation to model inter-channel interactions and temporal dependencies. Extensive experiments conducted on both a private clinical dataset and the public TUEV dataset demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in epileptic event detection. These results highlight its effectiveness in capturing clinically relevant EEG patterns and its potential for assisting automated epilepsy diagnosis.

source_records.title: UOT-GraphSSM: Unbalanced Optimal Transport Meets Graph State Space Models for Physics-Informed Spatio-temporal Traffic Forecasting
source_records.abstract: Spatio-temporal traffic forecasting still suffers from three linked limitations: balanced graph operators mismatch open road networks, sequence-style SSMs ignore real graph topology, and physics losses may become self-referential. We propose UOT-GraphSSM, which combines an unbalanced optimal transport (UOT) layer, a graph-native anisotropic SSM recurrence, and a stop-gradient CTM physics loss. The UOT layer produces a mass-relaxed asymmetric transport plan for directional boundary flux; the GraphSSM recurrence propagates hidden states along this plan rather than along a serialized node order; and the CTM loss provides non-circular physical regularisation. On PEMS04/07/08, UOT-GraphSSM achieves consistent state-of-the-art results, reducing MSE by 7–25%, lowering long-horizon degradation from 65% to 43%, and retaining a compact 1.6 M-parameter footprint.

source_records.title: KESTM: Knowledge-Enhanced Spatio-Temporal Module with Adaptive Gating for Dynamic Node Classification
source_records.abstract: Dynamic Graph Neural Networks (DGNNs) commonly utilize attention mechanisms to capture spatio-temporal dependencies. However, these methods often derive attention weights based on feature similarity, leading to an insufficient utilization of explicit topological evolution signals. This limitation hinders the model’s ability to perceive distinct structural roles within evolving graphs. To address this issue, we introduce Knowledge-Enhanced Spatio-Temporal ModuleKESTM (KES TM), a unified framework that bridges lightweight structural priors with adaptive spatio-temporal attention. KESTM comprises three key components: (1) a Knowledge Enhancement Module (KEM) that encodes multi-scale degree statistics and structural embeddings into learnable node-level priors; (2) an Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Encoder (ASTE) that employs a dual-stream attention mechanism with sparsity-aware gating to dynamically balance structural and temporal signals; and (3) a Dynamic Temporal-Contrastive Loss (DTCL) that jointly handles class imbalance and temporal inconsistency. Extensive experiments on four real-world dynamic graph benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. In particular, KESTM shows significant robustness under extreme graph sparsity, effectively addressing the Sparsity-Performance Paradox. Code is available at https://github.com/tyut2018/KESTM .

source_records.abstract: Accurate traffic forecasting requires effective modeling of complex spatio-temporal dependencies and reliable uncertainty estimation. source_records.title: A Physics-Informed Spatio-temporal Graph Learning Framework for EV Charging Demand Forecasting
source_records.abstract: Accurate forecasting of electric vehicle (EV) charging demand is essential for maintaining power-grid stability and supporting the efficient operation of urban charging infrastructure. However, EV charging demand exhibits strong spatio-temporal heterogeneity, multi-scale fluctuations, and complex dependencies, making accurate forecasting challenging. To address these issues, this paper proposes a physics-informed spatio-temporal graph learning framework for EV charging demand forecasting. Specifically, PSO-optimized MVMD is used to reconstruct multi-regional occupancy sequences, while a 2D-CNN is employed to capture temporal interaction patterns between occupancy and electricity price. A GAT-GFC-BiGRU-TPA architecture is then developed to model spatial dependencies and key temporal dynamics across charging regions. In addition, a physics-informed meta-learning strategy with a price-sensitivity regularization term is introduced to better capture the demand-response relationship between charging demand and electricity price while improving cross-region adaptability and training stability. Experiments on a real-world EV charging dataset show that the proposed framework consistently outperforms competitive baselines across multiple forecasting horizons. Ablation studies further verify the effectiveness of the major components. Overall, the proposed framework effectively captures complex spatio-temporal dynamics and improves short- and medium-term EV charging demand forecasting.

source_records.title: Dynamic Spatiotemporal Graph Learning of EEG for Multi-type Epileptiform Event Detection
source_records.abstract: Multi-type epileptiform events, including spike and ripple activities in electroencephalogram (EEG), are important biomarkers for seizure detection; however, their accurate detection is challenging due to complex spatio-temporal dynamics and multi-scale oscillatory patterns. To address these challenges, we propose a unified framework that integrates clinically motivated multi-band decomposition with dynamic spatio-temporal representation learning for accurate classification of EEG signals. Specifically, EEG signals are first decomposed into multiple frequency branches, followed by a branch-aware wavelet enhancement module to emphasize transient oscillatory patterns. A multi-scale temporal convolution module is then employed to capture diverse temporal dynamics across different time scales. Finally, a dynamic spatio-temporal graph reasoning module constructs sample-adaptive spatial and temporal graphs and performs joint propagation to model inter-channel interactions and temporal dependencies. Extensive experiments conducted on both a private clinical dataset and the public TUEV dataset demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in epileptic event detection. These results highlight its effectiveness in capturing clinically relevant EEG patterns and its potential for assisting automated epilepsy diagnosis.

source_records.title: UOT-GraphSSM: Unbalanced Optimal Transport Meets Graph State Space Models for Physics-Informed Spatio-temporal Traffic Forecasting
source_records.abstract: Spatio-temporal traffic forecasting still suffers from three linked limitations: balanced graph operators mismatch open road networks, sequence-style SSMs ignore real graph topology, and physics losses may become self-referential. We propose UOT-GraphSSM, which combines an unbalanced optimal transport (UOT) layer, a graph-native anisotropic SSM recurrence, and a stop-gradient CTM physics loss. The UOT layer produces a mass-relaxed asymmetric transport plan for directional boundary flux; the GraphSSM recurrence propagates hidden states along this plan rather than along a serialized node order; and the CTM loss provides non-circular physical regularisation. On PEMS04/07/08, UOT-GraphSSM achieves consistent state-of-the-art results, reducing MSE by 7–25%, lowering long-horizon degradation from 65% to 43%, and retaining a compact 1.6 M-parameter footprint.

source_records.title: KESTM: Knowledge-Enhanced Spatio-Temporal Module with Adaptive Gating for Dynamic Node Classification
source_records.abstract: Dynamic Graph Neural Networks (DGNNs) commonly utilize attention mechanisms to capture spatio-temporal dependencies. However, these methods often derive attention weights based on feature similarity, leading to an insufficient utilization of explicit topological evolution signals. This limitation hinders the model’s ability to perceive distinct structural roles within evolving graphs. To address this issue, we introduce Knowledge-Enhanced Spatio-Temporal ModuleKESTM (KES TM), a unified framework that bridges lightweight structural priors with adaptive spatio-temporal attention. KESTM comprises three key components: (1) a Knowledge Enhancement Module (KEM) that encodes multi-scale degree statistics and structural embeddings into learnable node-level priors; (2) an Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Encoder (ASTE) that employs a dual-stream attention mechanism with sparsity-aware gating to dynamically balance structural and temporal signals; and (3) a Dynamic Temporal-Contrastive Loss (DTCL) that jointly handles class imbalance and temporal inconsistency. Extensive experiments on four real-world dynamic graph benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. In particular, KESTM shows significant robustness under extreme graph sparsity, effectively addressing the Sparsity-Performance Paradox. Code is available at https://github.com/tyut2018/KESTM .

source_records.title: Direction-Aware Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks with Dual-Conditioned Normalizing Flows for Spatio-Temporal Anomaly Detection
source_records.abstract: Spatio-temporal graph neural networks on directed heterogeneous graphs face two structural challenges: symmetric graph aggregations cannot distinguish directional propagation mechanisms, and pure likelihood-based density scoring can underweight sparse localized perturbations. We address both within DA-GTNF, a unified framework for freeway anomaly detection. First, a direction-aware heterogeneous graph explicitly encodes four asymmetric relation types (downstream propagation, upstream shockwave, lateral lane interaction, and diagonal lane change), enabling a Relational GCN to learn independent aggregation kernels per relation. Second, a DualBranchGating mechanism fuses spatial graph embeddings and temporal Transformer embeddings through adaptive, feature-wise gates derived from unfused outputs. Third, a Dual-Conditioned Normalizing Flow estimates exact token-wise conditional log-likelihoods of the gated embeddings, while an auxiliary reconstruction head improves sensitivity to micro-level deviations that may be weakly reflected by NLL alone. On FT-AED, DA-GTNF achieves an AUC of 0.7218, a Reporting Delay of −11.80 min, a Mean Localization Error of 2.23 miles, and 100% incident coverage. On PeMS with incomplete ground truth, the segment-level DA-GTNF variant also consistently improves Recall@K% over all compared baselines.

source_records.title: Epidemiology-Informed Graph Neural Network for Heterogeneity-Aware Epidemic Forecasting
source_records.abstract: Among various spatio-temporal prediction tasks, epidemic forecasting plays a critical role in public health management. Recent studies have demonstrated the strong potential of spatio-temporal graph neural networks in extracting heterogeneous spatio-temporal patterns for epidemic forecasting. However, most of these methods bear an oversimplified assumption that two locations (e.g., cities) with similar observed features in previous time steps will develop similar infection numbers in the future. In fact, for any epidemic disease, there exists strong heterogeneity of its latent transmission dynamics across both geolocation and time, which can eventually lead to diverged infection numbers in two “similar” locations. However, capturing such latent transmission heterogeneity is non-trivial due to the existence of numerous influencing factors like medical resource accessibility, virus mutations, mobility patterns, etc., most of which are spatio-temporal yet unreachable or even unobservable. To address this challenge, we propose a Heterogeneous Epidemic-Aware Transmission Graph Neural Network (HeatGNN), a novel epidemic forecasting framework. By integrating epidemiological modeling into a Graph Neural Network, HeatGNN learns epidemiology-informed location embeddings of different locations that reflect their own transmission dynamics over time. On top of the conventional spatio-temporal module, a heterogeneous transmission graph network is designed to uncover the latent transmission heterogeneity among locations, where the time-varying latent transmission affinity graphs are computed on-the-fly and provide additional predictive signals. Experiments (Code is available at https://github.com/YufanZheng/HeatGNN_ECML-PKDD .) on four benchmark datasets have revealed that HeatGNN outperforms various strong baselines.

raw_metadata.abstract: Multi-type epileptiform events, including spike and ripple activities in electroencephalogram (EEG), are important biomarkers for seizure detection; however, their accurate detection is challenging due to complex spatio-temporal dynamics and multi-scale oscillatory patterns. To address these challenges, we propose a unified framework that integrates clinically motivated multi-band decomposition with dynamic spatio-temporal representation learning for accurate classification of EEG signals. Specifically, EEG signals are first decomposed into multiple frequency branches, followed by a branch-aware wavelet enhancement module to emphasize transient oscillatory patterns. A multi-scale temporal convolution module is then employed to capture diverse temporal dynamics across different time scales. Finally, a dynamic spatio-temporal graph reasoning module constructs sample-adaptive spatial and temporal graphs and performs joint propagation to model inter-channel interactions and temporal dependencies. Extensive experiments conducted on both a private clinical dataset and the public TUEV dataset demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in epileptic event detection. These results highlight its effectiveness in capturing clinically relevant EEG patterns and its potential for assisting automated epilepsy diagnosis.

source_records.title: UOT-GraphSSM: Unbalanced Optimal Transport Meets Graph State Space Models for Physics-Informed Spatio-temporal Traffic Forecasting
source_records.abstract: Spatio-temporal traffic forecasting still suffers from three linked limitations: balanced graph operators mismatch open road networks, sequence-style SSMs ignore real graph topology, and physics losses may become self-referential. We propose UOT-GraphSSM, which combines an unbalanced optimal transport (UOT) layer, a graph-native anisotropic SSM recurrence, and a stop-gradient CTM physics loss. The UOT layer produces a mass-relaxed asymmetric transport plan for directional boundary flux; the GraphSSM recurrence propagates hidden states along this plan rather than along a serialized node order; and the CTM loss provides non-circular physical regularisation. On PEMS04/07/08, UOT-GraphSSM achieves consistent state-of-the-art results, reducing MSE by 7–25%, lowering long-horizon degradation from 65% to 43%, and retaining a compact 1.6 M-parameter footprint.

source_records.title: KESTM: Knowledge-Enhanced Spatio-Temporal Module with Adaptive Gating for Dynamic Node Classification
source_records.abstract: Dynamic Graph Neural Networks (DGNNs) commonly utilize attention mechanisms to capture spatio-temporal dependencies. However, these methods often derive attention weights based on feature similarity, leading to an insufficient utilization of explicit topological evolution signals. This limitation hinders the model’s ability to perceive distinct structural roles within evolving graphs. To address this issue, we introduce Knowledge-Enhanced Spatio-Temporal ModuleKESTM (KES TM), a unified framework that bridges lightweight structural priors with adaptive spatio-temporal attention. KESTM comprises three key components: (1) a Knowledge Enhancement Module (KEM) that encodes multi-scale degree statistics and structural embeddings into learnable node-level priors; (2) an Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Encoder (ASTE) that employs a dual-stream attention mechanism with sparsity-aware gating to dynamically balance structural and temporal signals; and (3) a Dynamic Temporal-Contrastive Loss (DTCL) that jointly handles class imbalance and temporal inconsistency. Extensive experiments on four real-world dynamic graph benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. In particular, KESTM shows significant robustness under extreme graph sparsity, effectively addressing the Sparsity-Performance Paradox. Code is available at https://github.com/tyut2018/KESTM .

read_results.text: Spatio-temporal graph neural networks on directed heterogeneous graphs face two structural challenges: symmetric graph aggregations cannot distinguish directional propagation mechanisms, and pure likelihood-based density scoring can underweight sparse localized perturbations. We address both within DA-GTNF, a unified framework for freeway anomaly detection. First, a direction-aware heterogeneous graph explicitly encodes four asymmetric relation types (downstream propagation, upstream shockwave, lateral lane interaction, and diagonal lane change), enabling a Relational GCN to learn independent aggregation kernels per relation. Second, a DualBranchGating mechanism fuses spatial graph embeddings and temporal Transformer embeddings through adaptive, feature-wise gates derived from unfused outputs. Third, a Dual-Conditioned Normalizing Flow estimates exact token-wise conditional log-likelihoods of the gated embeddings, while an auxiliary reconstruction head improves sensitivity to micro-level deviations that may be weakly reflected by NLL alone. On FT-AED, DA-GTNF achieves an AUC of 0.7218, a Reporting Delay of −11.80 min, a Mean Localization Error of 2.23 miles, and 100% incident coverage. On PeMS with incomplete ground truth, the segment-level DA-GTNF variant also consistently improves Recall@K% over all compared baselines.

Dynamic Graph Neural Networks (DGNNs) commonly utilize attention mechanisms to capture spatio-temporal dependencies. However, these methods often derive attention weights based on feature similarity, leading to an insufficient utilization of explicit topological evolution signals. This limitation hinders the model’s ability to perceive distinct structural roles within evolving graphs. To address this issue, we introduce Knowledge-Enhanced Spatio-Temporal ModuleKESTM (KES TM), a unified framework that bridges lightweight structural priors with adaptive spatio-temporal attention. KESTM comprises three key components: (1) a Knowledge Enhancement Module (KEM) that encodes multi-scale degree statistics and structural embeddings into learnable node-level priors; (2) an Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Encoder (ASTE) that employs a dual-stream attention mechanism with sparsity-aware gating to dynamically balance structural and temporal signals; and (3) a Dynamic Temporal-Contrastive Loss (DTCL) that jointly handles class imbalance and temporal inconsistency. Extensive experiments on four real-world dynamic graph benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. In particular, KESTM shows significant robustness under extreme graph sparsity, effectively addressing the Sparsity-Performance Paradox. Code is available at https://github.com/tyut2018/KESTM .

Spatio-temporal traffic forecasting still suffers from three linked limitations: balanced graph operators mismatch open road networks, sequence-style SSMs ignore real graph topology, and physics losses may become self-referential. Among various spatio-temporal prediction tasks, epidemic forecasting plays a critical role in public health management. Recent studies have demonstrated the strong potential of spatio-temporal graph neural networks in extracting heterogeneous spatio-temporal patterns for epidemic forecasting. However, most of these methods bear an oversimplified assumption that two locations (e.g., cities) with similar observed features in previous time steps will develop similar infection numbers in the future. In fact, for any epidemic disease, there exists strong heterogeneity of its latent transmission dynamics across both geolocation and time, which can eventually lead to diverged infection numbers in two “similar” locations. However, capturing such latent transmission heterogeneity is non-trivial due to the existence of numerous influencing factors like medical resource accessibility, virus mutations, mobility patterns, etc., most of which are spatio-temporal yet unreachable or even unobservable. To address this challenge, we propose a Heterogeneous Epidemic-Aware Transmission Graph Neural Network (HeatGNN), a novel epidemic forecasting framework. By integrating epidemiological modeling into a Graph Neural Network, HeatGNN learns epidemiology-informed location embeddings of different locations that reflect their own transmission dynamics over time. On top of the conventional spatio-temporal module, a heterogeneous transmission graph network is designed to uncover the latent transmission heterogeneity among locations, where the time-varying latent transmission affinity graphs are computed on-the-fly and provide additional predictive signals. Experiments (Code is available at https://github.com/YufanZheng/HeatGNN_ECML-PKDD .) on four benchmark datasets have revealed that HeatGNN outperforms various strong baselines.

With the rapid development of IoT technologies and widespread deployment of intelligent sensing devices, dynamic sensor selection has become crucial for balancing recognition accuracy and energy efficiency in applications like health monitoring. Existing runtime assessment methods suffer from limited predictive utility for future sensor quality and fail to capture dynamic spatio-temporal dependencies among interconnected devices. To this end, we propose a utility-aware sensor selection framework that integrates adaptive spatio-temporal forecasting with attention-based quality assessment. Our approach employs a Dynamic Graph Learning-based Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (DGL-STGCN) to model evolving device correlations and predict sensor states, while an attention mechanism assesses future sensor utility through learned importance scores. This enables proactive sensor selection optimized for both recognition accuracy and energy consumption, explicitly accounting for switching overheads. We develop and evaluate a prototype system designed for wearable devices to monitor locomotion activities. Results show that our system achieves a 14% accuracy improvement over single-sensor baselines, a 25% reduction in energy consumption compared to full-sensor deployment, and a 2% higher accuracy than state-of-the-art methods at equivalent energy levels.

Accurate traffic forecasting requires effective modeling of complex spatio-temporal dependencies and reliable uncertainty estimation. Although existing graph-based methods have achieved strong performance, most focus on deterministic prediction and do not explicitly incorporate structural information into probabilistic modeling. In this paper, we propose HBPC-GWN, a hierarchical Bayesian calibration framework for graph-based traffic forecasting. Rather than imposing structural constraints during training, the proposed method performs posterior-level calibration by integrating a Laplacian-based prior into the predictive distribution. This enables a principled combination of data-driven predictions and graph-structured regularization, improving the consistency between spatial structure and uncertainty estimation. We instantiate the framework on Graph WaveNet and evaluate it on multiple real-world traffic datasets. Experimental results show that HBPC-GWN achieves competitive and more stable performance across forecasting horizons. In particular, it provides consistent improvements in medium- and long-term forecasting and improves probabilistic calibration, as reflected by better negative log-likelihood and prediction interval coverage. These results demonstrate that incorporating structural priors at the posterior level is an effective and flexible strategy for enhancing both predictive accuracy and uncertainty estimation in traffic forecasting.

Accurate forecasting of electric vehicle (EV) charging demand is essential for maintaining power-grid stability and supporting the efficient operation of urban charging infrastructure. However, EV charging demand exhibits strong spatio-temporal heterogeneity, multi-scale fluctuations, and complex dependencies, making accurate forecasting challenging. To address these issues, this paper proposes a physics-informed spatio-temporal graph learning framework for EV charging demand forecasting. Specifically, PSO-optimized MVMD is used to reconstruct multi-regional occupancy sequences, while a 2D-CNN is employed to capture temporal interaction patterns between occupancy and electricity price. A GAT-GFC-BiGRU-TPA architecture is then developed to model spatial dependencies and key temporal dynamics across charging regions. In addition, a physics-informed meta-learning strategy with a price-sensitivity regularization term is introduced to better capture the demand-response relationship between charging demand and electricity price while improving cross-region adaptability and training stability. Experiments on a real-world EV charging dataset show that the proposed framework consistently outperforms competitive baselines across multiple forecasting horizons. Ablation studies further verify the effectiveness of the major components. Overall, the proposed framework effectively captures complex spatio-temporal dynamics and improves short- and medium-term EV charging demand forecasting.
